advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the write-only sandbox scope (`(allow default)` + `(deny file-write*)`, `--ro-bind / /` with full read access and no network isolation) is an accepted limitation for running deliberately-broken mutant code, or extend to deny reads/network.
evidence: Docstring cites cargo-mutants recommending running 'in an isolated environment (container, CI, or VM)' (mutation_sandbox.py:11-13) but the profile only denies file-write*, leaving reads and network permitted under `(allow default)`.

ABSENCE: no `(deny network*)` or read restriction in build_seatbelt_profile; the bwrap path likewise binds `--ro-bind / /` (reads of whole FS allowed) with no network isolation (mutation_sandbox.py:146).
advisory.finding: The generated Seatbelt profile uses `(allow default)` with only `(deny file-write*)`, so the macOS sandbox restricts filesystem writes but leaves file reads and network access unrestricted; a destructive/malicious mutant executing under the sandbox can still read repository secrets or exfiltrate data over the network. This is narrower than the 'isolated environment' the module docstring cites, though it is a deliberate scoping to the deletion threat rather than a bright-line reachable exploit in the changed code.
scenarios: A mutant that reaches a code path making an outbound network call or reading credentials from the read-only-but-visible filesystem is not blocked by the write-only sandbox.

evidence: scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:87: `"(deny file-write*)",` with only allow-list subpaths plus /dev/{null,stdout,stderr,fd} re-permitted
ABSENCE: no allow entry for TMPDIR, `/tmp`, or `tempfile.gettempdir()` in either mechanism
advisory.finding: The sandbox allow-list contains only the scratch root and pytest basetemp; the system temp dir (TMPDIR/`/tmp`) is not writable. Under bwrap `--ro-bind / /` and the Seatbelt `(deny file-write*)` profile, any write to `/tmp` by pytest, mutmut, or an imported library (cache dirs, coverage data, tempfiles that don't honor --basetemp) is denied, which can cause spurious shard failures unrelated to mutation results.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure at least one gating CI lane installs a working sandbox mechanism (e.g. bubblewrap on Linux) so the @live enforcement assertions actually execute rather than skip.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:59-62: `live = pytest.mark.skipif(sb.probe() is None, reason="no OS sandbox mechanism on this host (sandbox-exec or bwrap)")`
tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py comment: `on Linux @live skips them because no workflow installs bubblewrap. That combination left the sandbox ENFORCEMENT unverified in CI entirely`
ABSENCE: no CI workflow in the diff installs bubblewrap on Linux, so on Linux gating lanes every enforcement assertion is skipped and a sandbox that denied nothing would still pass the suite there.
dropped.finding: The load-bearing @live enforcement tests (write-denied, rm -rf denied, mutmut-shape denied) are guarded by `@live = skipif(sb.probe() is None)`; on any gating lane without a working sandbox mechanism they all silently skip, so the actual OS-level write-deny is exercised only where a mechanism is present. Per the file's own docstring the Linux lane installs no bubblewrap, leaving enforcement verified only on the macOS platform_compat lane.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor to each deny/enforcement test (assert the sandboxed child actually ran — e.g. an expected non-zero exit from the denied write, or a PRESENCE marker written by the same child) before trusting `not target.exists()`.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:79 `assert not target.exists(), f"sandbox permitted a write outside the allow-list; {_why(proc)}"`
tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:108 `assert keep.exists(), f"sandbox permitted the destructive deletion; {_why(proc)}"`

`_why()` (line 56-58) renders returncode into the message but no test asserts `proc.returncode == 0` or otherwise proves the wrapped shell launched — the absence result is indistinguishable from 'the sandboxed child never started'.
dropped.finding: The sandbox-enforcement tests assert an absence (`not target.exists()`) derived from a sandboxed child process but never establish that the child actually ran — the subprocess returncode is captured only into the diagnostic `_why()` message string, never asserted. If `wrap()` produced an argv that fails to launch (e.g. `sandbox-exec` rejecting a malformed profile, a bwrap arg error), the target file is never created and the test passes green even though the sandbox enforced nothing — the exact fail-open failure the module exists to prevent.
scenarios: A regression in wrap()/build_seatbelt_profile that yields an argv sandbox-exec/bwrap refuses to start: the write never happens, `not target.exists()` is trivially true, the enforcement suite stays green while the sandbox enforces nothing.
dropped.suggested_fix: In the deny tests, have the wrapped command also write a liveness marker into the ALLOWED dir (or emit a sentinel to stdout) and assert that marker/sentinel is present, so a child that never launched fails the test instead of silently satisfying the absence assertion.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct docs/local-dev-env.md to state the venv is NOT writable in the sandbox (matching the deliberate exclusion of sys.prefix in execute_shard).
evidence: docs/local-dev-env.md:132: `filesystem writes outside the scratch tree, the pytest basetemp, and the venv.`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:594-596: `# sys.prefix is deliberately absent: a writable venv would let a mutant drop / # executable code into site-packages that later un-sandboxed phases import.`
scripts/mutation_gate.py:596: `sandbox_allow = (root, basetemp)` — venv/sys.prefix is not in the allow-list
scripts/mutation_sandbox.py:197-199: `# The venv is deliberately NOT writable (see execute_shard's allow-list)...`
dropped.finding: docs/local-dev-env.md claims the sandbox permits filesystem writes to 'the venv', but the code deliberately EXCLUDES the venv (sys.prefix) from the allow-list. An operator reading the doc would mis-diagnose a write-denied-in-site-packages failure as a bug rather than intended behavior.
dropped.suggested_fix: Change the doc sentence to 'denies filesystem writes outside the scratch tree and the pytest basetemp (the venv is deliberately read-only)'.
